en: We only just got married, you know.
note: Samantha (nurse) is newly married to Darrell; 'we' = she and her husband.

en: So we don't get many visitors.
Are you that curious about newlyweds?
No, it's not that.
But I never know when I'll need your care,
so I thought I'd come and say hello.
I'm sorry if I've disturbed you.
Well, when there are no patients,
we can keep you company, but...
For us, rather than healthy people, you see,
it's the patients we have to attend to.
Of course. I'm sorry for bothering you, then.
No, it's just... um, I wanted to see the place.
Just having a look around?
This isn't really a place healthy people
come to, so please don't stay too long.
Samantha...
Taking you away from your husband
note: Player, about to take Samantha as a servant; #8258 + #152 '...' follow.

en: pains me, but
I have to put an end to all this,
as soon as I possibly can
Please, give me any order you wish
note: Servant mode, after '{NAME}, my master.' and before #152 '...'.

en: Wha-, what on earth is this?
How unsightly, scratches everywhere. Horrid!
I've been waiting for you. Your orders
note: After '{NAME}, my master...'; #152 '...' follows. 'Master' not repeated.

en: I don't feel at all well, somehow
Oh, I'm so listless, so tired.
note: Same line after #8265 + #152 '...', so leading space.

en: Good day, madam.
Oh, and who might you be?
Forgive me, I can't seem to recall.
Pardon me. We have not met before, madam.
You seemed to glow in the soft sunlight,
so I could not help speaking to you.
I hope I gave no offense?
note: Same line after 'My name is {NAME}.' (#862/#473), so leading space.

en: My, you do have a way with words.
But then, people do often compliment me.
I'm Virginia. Pleased to meet you.
The pleasure is mine, madam.
Until we meet again, then.
Good day, my charming gentleman.
My, how fortunate. We meet again.
, isn't it?
Are you keeping well?
On business? I'm on my way to the beauty
salon now. How exciting, hee hee.
What lovely clothes you have on again today.
I've had a new dress made myself, you know.
It's the only pleasure I have.
A woman's life is so dull. Well, goodbye.
Good day, Arthur.
Oh, oh my, I'm sorry. Wrong person.
You're built just like someone I know.
Think nothing of it, madam.
To be greeted by so lovely a lady
is an honor, I assure you.
My, what a flatterer. But thank you.
My name is Virginia.
May I ask your name, if you don't mind?
Not at all.
My name is
, is it? Pleased to meet you.
note: After the name: '{NAME}, is it? Pleased to meet you.'

en: I'm sorry about earlier.
But I'm glad to have met such a lovely man.
, how are you keeping?
An evening stroll? Or is it a date?
How I envy you.
Once you get to be my age,
the joys of love are a distant memory.
There's no need to belittle yourself so.
Madam, you are still young.
Oh my, whatever shall I do?
You truly are a flatterer.
Oh, it's you. Good day.
We often meet at night, too, don't we?
Would you join me for some wine sometime?
Will you call on me when you're in the mood?
Oh my, how rare, a man in a beauty salon.
You must be quite the stylish gentleman.
Hello, madam.
It seems I have come to the wrong house.
